_meta.purpose: Canonical D1 REST API request/response schema + hard-won gotchas. Read BEFORE any D1 query/insert/update to avoid repeated failures already root-caused in prior sessions.

step_1_account_id.note: ALWAYS get the live account ID this way. NEVER hardcode or guess -- a wrong account ID produces a misleading 401/404 indistinguishable from a real permission problem.

step_2_database_uuid.note: NEVER hardcode a database UUID either -- always re-verify fresh.

step_3_binding_check.note: wrangler d1 execute <name> --remote FAILS with 'Couldn't find a D1 DB with name/binding' unless that name is bound in a LOCAL wrangler.toml/wrangler.jsonc. For shared infra DBs with no local binding (e.g. living-paper), use the REST API directly instead of the CLI.

params: array of bound values, in order

gotchas: ON CONFLICT upsert against a table with FTS5 shadow tables (e.g. living-paper.papers has papers_fts*) returned HTTP 400 in production testing. Use CHECK-THEN-WRITE instead: SELECT existence first, then a plain INSERT (no ON CONFLICT) or plain UPDATE -- never a combined upsert on such tables.
A single successful INSERT on an FTS5-triggered table can report changes > 1 due to trigger fan-out -- this is expected, NOT a duplicate-row bug.

Column names must be verified, not assumed: run SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='<table>' then PRAGMA table_info(<table>) if unsure. (Known gotcha: living-paper.papers uses body_md, not body.)

Large body_md string writes via inline PowerShell JSON construction (ConvertTo-Json) have corrupted content in past sessions (stored literal '[object Object]' string, 15 bytes, instead of the actual 47KB content). ROOT CAUSE: PowerShell's ConvertTo-Json mis-serializing a large multi-line string with embedded YAML/markdown special characters when piped through curl.exe with a temp JSON file. FIX: use Node.js (fs.readFileSync + JSON.stringify + https.request) instead of PowerShell string-building for any D1 write payload larger than a few hundred characters. Verify by reading back LENGTH(body_md) and comparing to local file byte count -- do not trust the 'success:true, changes:N' response wrapper alone.

verification_gate.rule: After ANY INSERT/UPDATE, re-run a SELECT against the exact row/column just written and compare byte length or content hash to the source. A 'success:true' wrapper on the write response is NOT verification (Anti-Phantom Gate, qnfo-agent Rule 14).
verification_gate.example: SELECT LENGTH(body_md) as blen FROM papers WHERE slug = ? -- compare blen to len(local_file_content)

backup_before_destructive_ops.rule: Before any D1 Time Travel restore, export a full row/table snapshot (explicit column list, avoid FTS5 tables which break d1 export) to R2 as a safety net FIRST.
